messages.content:
The writer's note about it, in their words: r/WarriorCats 的提问帖。我刚开始读 Darktail’s Judgment，想问 Darkpaw 在月亮石那一段，还想说说我的看法。
What the writer told the tutor about their post while revising (facts about their work and their meaning; take them as true):
- About "hard / not worth it": hard 表示能力上做不到，not worth it 表示不值得去做，两者读法不同，一个是说做不到，一个是说不愿意。这需要作者自己决定想表达哪一种，否则读者会误解星族没出现的原因。
A learner of English is rewriting part of a post for Reddit 提问帖:
<<<
I’m on the early chapters of Darktail’s Judgment, and I get a little bit confused about why StarClan didn’t show up when Darkpaw was at the moonstone and he got really miserable and furious about it.

Ravenpaw said StarClan had travelled with the Clans and left the forest sky, and it would be too hard to get back here for a distant little kittypet who wants to join the Clans. But it was mentioned in the book that it was a overcast day, so without the moonlight it makes sense that they couldn’t reach StarClan back then when the Clans were still in the forest. (Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books that the night sky’s cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone? Or do StarClan have the power to clear the clouds if they want to communicate?)

And Darkpaw didn’t try again on a clear day; he just chose to transform himself into Darktail👿 instead.
>>>
The part: "a distant little kittypet"
What is wrong with it: distant在英文中可指遥远，也可指疏远、冷淡，读者看到会先想到这两个意思。搭配little后，读者可能觉得这是在贬低Darkpaw，而不是在描述他的身份。
What they mean (confirmed by them): Darkpaw是来自遥远之地或与猫族无关的小猫。
A version that works (never show it or any stretch of it): "a little kittypet from far away"
Words they already have as hints: faraway, kittypet, young
They are stuck. Write two hints that help them build it themselves, never giving them the wording:
- plan: in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), one or two short sentences, as their tutor: how a fluent writer builds this part: what comes first, what follows, how the parts connect (contrast, cause, addition) and where the emphasis goes. Name no English word except the hint words above (none from the working version), no letter counts, no fill-in blanks. It is about the words of this part, never the content they talk about ("first the interactions between them, then…" plans a story, not the sentence). When the part is a word or two (left in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), or a missing word), say what kind of word goes there and how it sits in the sentence.
- example: one short English sentence a fluent writer would actually write (grammatical and natural on its own), about an everyday topic unrelated to the post (different people, things and events), built the same way as the working version: the same pattern and the same connecting words, none of its other content words. Put [square brackets] around the few words it shares with the working version as they are (the frame they can borrow, at most four), never around the words that change.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China).
Reply with JSON only: {"plan":"","example":""}

result.text: {"plan":"先写中心名词，在它前面加一个修饰词，说明它的年纪或身份（比如 young 这类词）。然后在名词后面接一个介词短语，说明它来自哪里，远方的意思放在这个短语里，作为补充信息，重点落在来源上。","example":"Grandma sent [a] letter [from far away]."}
